definitions: To add a final, often negative or surprising, element to a series of events.
To conclude a sequence of events, especially with something that makes the situation even better or worse.
examples: First my car broke down, then I lost my wallet, and to top it all off, it started raining.
The food was delicious, the company was great, and to top it all off, they brought out a surprise cake.
He missed his flight, his luggage got lost, and to top it all off, he realized he'd forgotten his passport.
